exposure: low pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A) levels (< 0.4 multiple of median)
cohort: 1640 consecutive pregnant women recruited between 9+5 and 13+6 weeks of pregnancy, with 130 women having low PAPP-A levels (cases) and 200 women with normal PAPP-A levels (controls) followed until delivery.
finding: Women with low PAPP-A levels had a significantly higher incidence of intrauterine growth restriction, preterm birth, and low birthweight compared to controls.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome (low-birthweight babies reported)
gest_age: Recruitment: 9+5 to 13+6 weeks; Preterm birth was an outcome.
